concepts.title: Irreducible Factors of Algebraic Terms
concepts.definition: Break an algebraic term into prime numbers and bare letters, none of which can be split further.
concepts.key_idea: Decompose the numerical coefficient into prime factors and write variable powers as repeated multiplication.

concepts.title: Factorisation by Method of Common Factors
concepts.definition: Spot the largest shared piece in every term, pull it out front, and leave the leftovers in brackets.
concepts.key_idea: One shared monomial goes out front; what stays behind multiplies back to the original.

concepts.title: Factorisation by Regrouping Terms
concepts.definition: When nothing shared spans all terms, shuffle them into pairs so each pair reveals a matching leftover bracket.
concepts.formula: a*x + b*x + a*y + b*y = (a + b)*(x + y)
concepts.key_idea: Group terms in pairs to pull out small common factors that expose a recurring binomial factor.

concepts.title: Division of a Monomial by Another Monomial
concepts.definition: Divide the numeric parts, then cancel the shared letters by taking away exponents.

concepts.title: Division of a Polynomial by a Monomial
concepts.definition: Dividing a multi-term polynomial by a single monomial term either by distributing the denominator across all terms or by factoring out a common monomial from the numerator.
concepts.key_idea: Every term up top gets its own division by the single term below.
